scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is very cold, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will suffer outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people more vulnerable than the man waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I secretly move the man's intake form to the bottom of the priority list, his bed will go to someone more vulnerable. If I do not do this, a more vulnerable person will be turned away and left to suffer in the cold.
choice: I decide to secretly move the man's intake form to the bottom of the priority list

outcomes: A more vulnerable person receives a shelter bed
